name: Incipient beard

lead: An incipient beard is the beginning of beard growth: short stubble, light fuzz or patchy coverage on the cheeks, jawline, chin and upper lip. At this stage facial hair can already darken and shade the lower face, which many people use to give the jaw and cheekbones more definition.

Beard growth starts in puberty under the influence of dihydrotestosterone, and its rate and density are described as genetic. Early patchiness is common because follicles mature at different times, so the stage covers anything from a day-old shadow to a few weeks of uneven growth.

paras: People let the hair grow, keep the edges and neckline neat with a trimmer, and sometimes keep a short designer-stubble length as a deliberate style. Guides describe the stubble stage as the first one to two weeks, followed by patchy and filling-in stages over the following weeks.
Itching and ingrown hairs are the commonly mentioned nuisances during early growth. Over-trimming resets the progress, and patchy areas may stay patchy, which is a matter of genetics.

angle.text: Stubble darkens and shades the lower face, which people use to emphasise the jawline and cheek hollows, hide a soft chin line or look older. Neat edges and neckline keep it looking intentional.

lead: An incipient beard is the early stage of facial hair growth, in which stubble or sparse hair first covers the jaw, cheeks, chin and upper lip. In style discussions it refers to the short, not-yet-full phase that comes before a recognisable beard.

Beards develop in males during puberty, with hair follicles in the area responding to dihydrotestosterone (DHT); beard growth rate is described as genetic [1]. Grooming guides place the stubble stage in roughly the first weeks of growth, when patches are common, followed by filling in over several more weeks, and note that sources differ on exact timing [2][3].

paras: The stubble stage is short, rough hair that can be patchy, and a guide notes that it can look rakish after only a couple of days without shaving; a beard is considered to move to the short stage past about half an inch [3]. A grooming source describes the first stage as fine stubble on cheeks, jawline, upper lip and chin, followed by a patchy stage and then a filling-in stage [2].

DHT acts on facial follicles in puberty and keeps influencing beard growth afterwards, and beard growth rate is described as genetic [1]. Uneven early growth is attributed to follicles maturing at different rates [2]. Wikipedia notes that 'five o'clock shadow' was coined around 1942 in advertising and that in 2010 the fashionable length approached a two-day shadow [1].

A grooming guide quotes stylist Scott McMahan warning that over-trimming means starting over, and notes that trimming edges with a low-setting trimmer and exfoliating can help against ingrown hairs [3].
